text:
Slightly Lower Ahead of Fed Decision 01-Aug-18 13:00 ET Dow -66.35 at 25348.84, Nasdaq +17.23 at 7689.02, S&P -4.47 at 2811.56
[BRIEFING.COM] The market began today's session on a positive note following an upbeat earnings report and guidance from Apple (AAPL 199.94, +9.65), but an intraday reversal from the heavily-weighted financial sector leaves the S&P 500 modestly lower (-0.2%) ahead of the Fed's rate decision, which will cross the wires at 2:00 PM ET.
Apple has rallied 5.2% today, hitting a new all-time high, after reporting better-than-expected earnings and revenues for its fiscal third quarter on Tuesday evening and after issuing above-consensus guidance for Q4. Its upbeat report has helped restore faith in high-flying FAANG names, which have been lagging since Facebook's (FB 172.07, -0.51) disappointing earnings release last Thursday. The top-weighted information technology sector is up 0.8%.
The financial space was up with technology at the start of today's session, trading as high as +1.1%, but has since slipped into the red, now down 0.1%. The reversal followed news that Fidelity will be offering new index funds with zero fees, creating concerns over the future profitability of competitors like BlackRock (BLK 481.37, -21.38, -4.3%) and T. Row Price (TROW 115.83, -3.25, -2.7%).
Most other sectors are currently in the red and have been for the entirety of today's session; even when financials were strong, seven of eleven groups were in the red.
The trade-sensitive industrial sector (-1.1%) is among the worst performers following reports that the Trump administration is considering more than doubling planned tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods, raising the levies to 25% from 10%. Energy (-1.6%) is also lagging, weighed down by a 1.4% decline in WTI crude futures ($67.79/bbl).
Elsewhere, U.S. Treasuries are under pressure, pushing yields higher across the curve; the yield on the benchmark 10-yr Treasury note is up four basis points at 3.00%. The U.S. Dollar Index is up modestly, rising 0.1% to 94.44, and the CBOE Volatility Index is higher by 5.5% at 13.53.
The Fed isn't expected to announce a rate hike this afternoon, but investors will still be looking for clues on future rate hikes. The market is currently pricing in two more rate hikes by the year's end, and that's on top of the two rate hikes announced earlier this year.
Reviewing today's economic data, which included the ADP Employment Change report for July, the Construction Spending report for June, the ISM Index for July, and the weekly MBA Mortgage Applications Index: The ADP National Employment Report showed an increase of 219,000 in July (Briefing.com consensus 175,000), and the June reading was revised to 181,000 from 177,000. The ADP reading is seen as a prelude to the BLS's nonfarm payrolls figure (Briefing.com consensus 190,000), which will be released on Friday. The ISM Index for July decreased to 58.1 from an unrevised reading of 60.2 in June, while the Briefing.com consensus expected a reading of 59.4. The key takeaway from the report is that manufacturing demand is strong, evidenced by the 15th straight month the New Orders Index has been 60% or higher. Construction spending declined 1.1% in June (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%), and the May reading was revised to +1.3% from +0.4%. The key takeaway from the report is that the upward revision to spending in May mitigated most of the headline disappointment for June, which implies the June downturn is not as bad as it appears at first blush. The weekly MBA Mortgage Applications Index decreased 2.6% to follows last week's downtick of 0.2%.
